constants_godot_room_space.axes: x right, y up, -z forward; az = atan(x, -z), el = asin(y)
constants_godot_room_space.sun_note: 74.0 deg from planet_direction at the same azimuth: 1.9 deg inside the disk edge, behind the limb at its highest point (az -45, el 19.9), which is the left edge of the front-left pane; never drawn
constants_godot_room_space.twilight: d2 = depth^2; inside_deg = d2*(108.17 + d2*(-215.83 + d2*338.51)), a fit within .07 deg over the band; tw = exp(-inside_deg/2.2)*(1-smoothstep(5,9,inside_deg))*exp(limb_fall*(dot(normal,sun)+.033))

galaxy_basis.note: A true great circle with the galactic centre at az 57, el 80, leaning 24 deg in the up view, with longitude falling upward; the 2026-11-02 basis turned by -24 deg about the up view, then slid -55 deg about the galactic pole. prepare_stars.py and prepare_objects.py read the same basis.

constants_godot_room_space.bake_proxy: build_runtime.py earth_proxy tests the same sphere with the room ray as it is and applies the same twilight fade (TWILIGHT_FADE_DEG); starship.json sky records planet_direction, planet_distance, sun and twilight_fade_deg, and check_integration.py compares them with this shader's defaults

cap_atlas.projection: azimuthal cap, radius 16 deg of surface angle, centred on n0; row 0 = +north; logarithmic radius r = ln(1 + rho/rho0)/ln(1 + 16/rho0); geographic angle = geo_scale x surface angle along the same bearing
cap_atlas.shader_uv: s = (dot(n,east), dot(n,north)); ang = atan(|s|, dot(n,n0)); uv = .5 + (s.x,-s.y)*ln(1 + ang/radians(2.5))/ln(7.4)*.5/max(|s|,1e-5)
cap_atlas.sub_viewer_choice: Round Earth pass: moving the centre to az -45 turned the whole atlas with it, so the sub-viewer and heading were picked again by a search over (lat, lon, heading) for lit strings in the hero window and the side panes, then from renders: 37.0N 69.0W, heading -90 (the view looks west from off the eastern seaboard, so north is to the right). The hero window shows the Mississippi and Ohio valley town networks (St Louis at az -33 el 13, Chicago just behind the housing edge at az -22 el 10), the next pane left Atlanta, New Orleans and Houston (az -54 to -60), and the pane after it the Florida peninsula and Havana (az -77 to -89). 30N 74W h-60 keeps the old hero within 0.75 deg of screen position at the median but leaves the side panes emptier and puts Atlanta, magnified, in a large hot blob low in the window (817 warm px against 195). The geography is real and unmirrored, and two runs give byte-identical PNGs.
cap_atlas.mirror_assert: London -> Rome -> Moscow cross product in atlas pixels (y down) must be negative; it is for every candidate
cap_atlas.filter: Catmull-Rom bicubic (a=-0.5), 16 taps, x wrapped, y clamped, 2x2 supersampled and box-averaged per atlas texel, chunks of atlas rows; masks derived after resampling

masks.R: cloud coverage (window ring densified by a second sample, unsharp-masked for relief)
masks.G: city lights from the 500 m tiles (threads and hubs, cubed by the shader, softened by a last small blur of the light; 3 km fallback outside the tiles)

cloud_second_sample.heading_note: Heading -17: the hero window moved 17 deg round the limb with the centre, so this keeps the same cloud band across it. A cloud sample only; the geography is unaffected.

city_lights.note: real light only, no random numbers: local contrast of the peak-leaning area statistic, weighted by line evidence and regional light, plus one hot core per bright area (see city_lights)

cap_atlas.city_filter: Exact area coverage: every lit 500 m pixel lands in the atlas texel that holds its centre, weighted by its true area, and the sums are divided by the texel's geographic area (a texel covers 6-20 source pixels a side). The 3 km map fills the part of the cap outside the tiles, which only a viewer leaning low can see: 0.06% of the rays down to 12 deg below the horizon, none of those above it.
cap_atlas.retired: Shipped up to 0.5.11; prepare_earth.py --cap still builds it, but no runtime file comes from it now.

mapping.u: galactic longitude, lon = (u - .5)*360 deg, centre at u = .5

galaxy.coupling: The band is a true great circle: its path in the room is the shader's galaxy basis alone. prepare_stars.py reads the same basis; change it there, then rerun prepare_stars.py. Stored 1 / galaxy_exposure up.
galaxy.source: NASA/Goddard SVS Deep Star Maps 2020, milkyway_2020_8k_gal, through prepare_dust.py: the smooth glow of unresolved stars at 3 deg, printed stars filled in from their surround, the edge following the map's own isophotes
galaxy.deterministic: same map, same constants, same arrays; prepare_dust.py pins the source hash and two runs gave the same hashes

shader.masks: earth-masks.res (R city lights, squared by the shader, G water; BC7, repeat), sampled filter_linear_mipmap_anisotropic
shader.galaxy: galaxy.res (BC6H, repeat in u), the smooth glow
shader.set_by_room: starship_room.gd binds surface, masks, clouds, detail, galaxy and dust and sets world_to_room on recenter. earth_spin and earth_gain are global shader uniforms, so moving them does not re-render the radiance map. The room dimmer reaches neither the stars nor the Milky Way.

stars.mesh: stars.dat (prepare_stars.py): direction chunks of small additive triangles in the transparent pass, depth test on, w = 0 clip position (true infinity), each triangle baked as directions, so the kernel is fixed in angle
stars.eye_depth: DEPTH_HERO, DEPTH_MID, DEPTH_DUST, 0 in this build; radians per eye; never negative

shader.band: a smooth glow seen through dust, in the fixed galactic basis: the dust, a soft hue-keeping black point before the grain, then a tone (TONE_TOP, TONE_KNEE, BAND_TINT). It follows earth_gain. The fetches sit below the Earth's coverage. Half a 10-bit step of panel-fixed noise stays on the Earth and in its glare; sky_panel_noise 1 extends it to the whole sky, for the head test
shader.background: true black: nothing behind the Milky Way and the stars
shader.notes: No TIME. AT_CUBEMAP_PASS returns black. Plain texture() on the cap atlas (anisotropic on masks); seam-safe textureGrad only on the galaxy. Added in the look pass: one log() for the cap radius, about a dozen ALU for the night shading, anisotropic filtering on the masks sampler (Earth branch only), one extra multiply per bright star. Removed: the bright-star bloom exp. Texture fetches per pixel unchanged. Final look pass: about 4 ALU for the grazing cloud fade (one dot, one smoothstep, one mix); constants changed (twilight colour and weight, cloud ramp, city curve and day cut-off, halo colours, star density and tint); texture fetches unchanged. Galaxy refit (2026-11-02 v7): constants only (basis, galaxy_exposure 120 -> 1.25 for the 100x stored scale); texture size, format, fetches and ALU unchanged. Night lights (2026-11-02 v8): pow(G, 2.2) became G*G*G, plus one mix, one smoothstep and one max for the colour and the level cap; no uniform, texture fetch or draw call added. Round Earth (2026-11-02 v9): removed the warp and the limb drop (one atan, one asin, two smoothsteps, a sine and a cosine, a length and a clamp per fragment); no fetch, uniform or texture byte added. Turning Earth (0.5.12): textureGrad on three belt maps and one atan in place of the cap atlas and its log; one exp for the air; one exp each for the band and the rim; normalize and cross replaced by constants; the fetches stop at edge .004. Real sky (0.5.12): the lattice stars and the navy fill left the shader; the stars are one mesh, stars.gdshader.
shader.night_side: moonlit = .4 + .6*max(dot(n, moon), 0); land (.12 + mix(grey, ground, .35))*moon_color*1.25, ocean (.0036,.0085,.0230), cloud tops (.024,.042,.110)*(.3 + .7*thick^2) with cloud = smoothstep(.12,.88,thick); times (1 - day); then the air: planet *= (sqrt(clear), clear, clear^2), planet += (.007,.016,.040)*(1-clear)*moonlit, clear = exp(-.10/(depth+.05))
shader.twilight: tw = exp(-max(inside,0)/3.5)*(1 - smoothstep(5, 9, inside))*max(.85, sun_side); band = (.08 + .92*cloud)*(.13,.31,.92)*tw*twilight_gain: clear ocean takes 8% of the band, so the limb reads deep blue with lit clouds on it
shader.cities: The lights are one mesh of points, cities.gdshader and cities.dat (prepare_cities.py): the ground geography run backwards with earth_spin, a round kernel fixed in angle, a cloud fetch in the vertex stage on the same shell as the sky. The size of a light is fixed by its own amplitude; its skirt reads the light before the dimmer of the room, so nothing changes shape while it fades and a metro keeps its glow in Focus. The map keeps only a low glow: city_glow .14, LOD 3 of the city channel, with the same air and night terms.
shader.earth_geometry: One rigid sphere: along = dot(center, ray), miss = length(center - along*ray), with ray the room ray as it is (world_to_room is orthonormal). Earth disk, halo, glare and twilight all use it.
shader.clouds: earth-clouds.res (R clouds, G a second cloud sample for the window ring; BC7, repeat) on a shell 19 km up (CLOUD_H): three taps, the cloud at a footprint of 1.41-1.91x, one a step toward the moon, one 3 mips up that sets the threshold, the tops and a soft low deck. cloud-detail.res (one channel, BC4) bites the edges of real cloud within 9 deg of the limb.

global_uniforms.earth_spin: vec2, turns of longitude for ground and clouds, wrapped to 0-1 and advanced by starship_room.gd every frame
global_uniforms.earth_gain: float, 1.0 at the default light and above, down to .55 at Focus, on a 15 s ramp from starship_room.gd
global_uniforms.declared: both in project.godot [shader_globals], and at run time by starship_room.gd declare_sky_globals() for stages whose project.godot has no such entry

shader.dust: dust.res (BC5, repeat in u), optical depth and fine grain, rows |sin b| < .3

objects.mesh: objects.dat: star triangles and tangent-plane quads reading objects-atlas.res. Premultiplied alpha, so an object's dust hides what lies behind it
objects.focus: light follows earth_gain, stars sqrt(earth_gain); dust hides what it hides at any gain

shader.field: a faint field off the band, in the sky shader: at most one tiny star per cell of a cube grid on the galactic basis, at a hashed place, FWHM .138 deg, peak FIELD_LOW to FIELD_TOP, clumped by slow waves, following sqrt(earth_gain). No map and no triangle. Its positions are invented

rebuild_tools: prepare_earth.py --belt --download-tiles  (defaults: GEO_SCALE 3, first view 37N 64W with room north at bearing -90). Makes earth-surface.png and earth-masks.png. Its 8192x2048 earth-clouds.png is not the shipped one
python -I build_cloud_belt.py <1 km folder> <maps>, from outside the data folder, and rename earth-clouds-8192x2880.png to earth-clouds.png
python make_cloud_tile.py --output <maps>  (the defaults are the shipped tile)

python -I prepare_dust.py --work <folder holding mw8kgal.npy, band_stars.npz> --out <dir>, then pack_final.gd twice: galaxy.raw 4096 1024 glow galaxy.res, dust.raw 8192 1024 dust dust.res. Writes lane_field.npy and shown_glow.npy for the star mesh
python -I prepare_mw_peaks.py, once, then python -I prepare_stars.py  (reads Yale, stars_extracted.npz, open_sky.npz, mw_peaks.npz, lane_field.npy, shown_glow.npy; each pinned by hash)
prepare_objects.py --stage <stage>  (objects.dat and objects-atlas.res, after stars.dat, because it drops doubles of it; its volume tools and cached sprites are kept outside the app folder)
copy earth-surface.res, earth-masks.res, earth-clouds.res, cloud-detail.res and galaxy.res into project/starship (the receipt stays next to the inputs)
verify_limb.py  (sky-only renders in every direction, a circle fitted to the limb on the unit sphere; writes verification/limb-round.json)

stars.note: Tiers: hero, mid and clouds, dust. Every star at V 6.5 or brighter comes from the Yale Bright Star Catalogue. Clouds and dust are real peaks of the NASA Milky Way map, at real places, thinned by the shown band (shown_glow.npy) and the lanes (lane_field.npy); their brightness comes from peak rank, not from real magnitudes, and their tints are an assigned spread. So only their positions are strictly real. Chunked by direction; the limb is baked.

belt.why: The Earth should turn very slowly. The cap atlas ran out 1.9 deg past the horizon and could not turn; a wrapped latitude belt can turn for any number of hours.
belt.projection: wrapped longitude, u = lon/360 + .5; latitude -6 to 80, v = (sin(top) - sin(lat)) / (sin(top) - sin(bottom)); row 0 = north

turn.direction: true: surface moving east, ground comes out of the limb toward the viewer
turn.clock: Time.get_ticks_usec, so each launch opens on the first view
turn.changed_2026_11_05: 0.5.15: 150 deg/h, five times 0.5.14's 30 and about ten times the true rate, after the 2026-11-04 test room. Only EARTH_DEG_PER_HOUR moved: the maps, size, limb, first view and the clouds' 1.08x are 0.5.14's.

speed_150_calc.note: calibration_turning_earth_2026_11_02.measured_pc_renders.speed_30_deg_h times five, by arithmetic, not measured

belt.not_covered_by_500m_tiles: East of 0 and south of the equator stay on the 3 km map, with a 1.5 deg feather at the tile edges.

dust.source: The same map through prepare_dust.py. R: optical depth from the real map by non-local means, lanes and knots at three scales, with a fixed-seed tear of up to about .2 deg; the big lanes stay real. G: clumps of real faint stars

shader.order: black point on the depth alone, then the grain

dust.note: An unbound dust map reads black: no error, and the band goes bright. It is only read on rows |sin b| < .3.

objects.source: Procedural: numpy 3D volumes and Monte Carlo star clouds at real J2000 places. No image is sampled. The outline, knot places and cluster places of the Magellanic Clouds are real; individual stars are synthetic
